authority.abi: Diff lines containing no_mangle, repr(C) or export_name: 0. Every exported symbol and signature is unchanged. FILE/LINE are unchanged: crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c, 0. The only new extern "C" line is a test-only callback inside #[cfg(test)].
authority.allocator_seam: The new ContentHandoff Drop calls CRYPTO_free at the existing FILE/LINE (crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c, 0), the same seam and coordinates the removed Collected::adopt path used. No seam constant, size, file or line changed; there is one additional call site in the handoff guard.
authority.behaviour: Header ordering, the cached TOO_LONG test before the header error bit, constructed-string collection, indefinite EOC walks, per-arm reason codes and the decoded-value publication rule are preserved. One deliberate divergence is recorded below for a failing EXTERN hook.

scope_item_1_partial_object_ownership.verdict: No normal-return failure path was found that leaks or double-owns. Two defects existed and are fixed: an unwinding handoff leaked, and the free_cont flag was a Rust bool handed to a C char* hook.
scope_item_1_partial_object_ownership.PushedElements: Audited unchanged. The guard owns exactly the elements it pushed (the stack was emptied first), frees an element the stack refuses, pops/frees on failure, and disarms on commit. The stack itself is owned by the value (or by the direct-entry caller). Its multi-push failure behaviour is now pinned by d2i_sequence_of_failure_after_several_elements_owns_nothing.
scope_item_1_partial_object_ownership.already_assigned_fields: A field assigned before a later failure is released by item_ex_d2i_intern's ASN1_item_ex_free (the indirect entry) or by the direct caller (x509_pubkey_ex_d2i_ex frees on ret <= 0). The object is not left installed: the slot is nulled (indirect) or owned by the caller that must free it (direct).
scope_item_1_partial_object_ownership.cached_encoding: enc_save runs immediately before the POST callback. On a POST failure the value is freed by ASN1_item_ex_free -> item_embed_free -> enc_free, which releases the cached block before the value itself, and the slot is nulled. d2i_nested_encoded_template_failure_leaves_no_cached_value proves the decode reached enc_save (recorded non-null cache at POST), then failed, then left no value at all; a retry decodes from a clean slot.

take_raw_handoff.pre_fix: Collected::take_raw cleared the owner; the block was reclaimed with an unsafe Collected::adopt only on a normal return from ex_c2i. An unwind out of ex_c2i left the block owned by nobody.
take_raw_handoff.fix: ContentHandoff owns the block from take_raw until after ex_c2i. Its Drop releases it unless the codec cleared free_cont, so normal failure, success-without-consumption and unwinding all release exactly once. Collected::adopt (unsafe fn) is removed.

free_cont_validity.defect: The flag was a Rust bool whose address was cast to the prim_c2i hook's char*. A conforming C hook may store any char, after which reading the slot as bool is an invalid-value read (UB).
free_cont_validity.fix: The flag is c_char throughout (d2i_ex_primitive, ex_c2i, ContentHandoff); any non-zero byte means the codec still owns the block, zero means it took it. The hook now receives free_cont as *mut c_char with no cast through bool.

scope_item_2_lifetime_bound_input.boundary: One Cursor is derived at each exported/internal entry point from the caller's (pointer, len) contract: item_d2i, ASN1_item_ex_d2i, ASN1_item_d2i_ex and asn1_item_embed_d2i.
scope_item_2_lifetime_bound_input.interior: embed_d2i, mstring_d2i, template_ex_d2i, template_noexp_d2i and d2i_ex_primitive now take &mut Cursor. No interior function takes a raw input pointer plus a separate length, so no interior function can re-derive an extent. Each works on a local copy and commits the caller's cursor only on success, preserving 'no progress on failure'.
scope_item_2_lifetime_bound_input.removed: cursor_distance and remaining_after are deleted (15 use sites). Nine interior Cursor::new constructor calls are gone; four boundary constructors replace them.
remaining_raw_pairs: An ASN1_ITYPE_EXTERN asn1_ex_d2i/asn1_ex_d2i_ex hook: a genuine ABI edge. The pair is derived once from the cursor and folded back with advance_to on success; an over-advance is refused.

ex_c2i's content pointer plus length: the content-codec seam. A primitive's prim_c2i hook and the detached ossl_c2i_* codecs take (const unsigned char *, long) by contract; the pointer and length are single-sourced from the cursor and proved by take/limit/advance before the call.
scope_item_2_lifetime_bound_input.representation_choice: The module's S41 Cursor (pointer plus remaining count) is the lifetime-bounded view, rather than a materialised &[u8]: the decoder must track mutable progress and publish a raw pointer at the ABI, and a second shared-slice view over allocator-owned content would add provenance/aliasing constraints without enforcing anything the cursor does not.

scope_item_3_asn1_get_object.verdict: SOUND AS A READER; no change made to src/asn1/der.rs.
proof: max starts at omax and is decremented in lockstep with every p advance; every read is guarded by max >= 1, so p never exceeds start + omax.
asn1_get_length returns 0 on any length-byte overrun, and its definite-length accumulation refuses a value above c_long::MAX.
consumed = p - start is therefore in [0, omax], so omax - consumed cannot underflow; the comparison only raises the recoverable 0x80 flag and sets ret |= 0x80.
*pp is published at p even on the TOO_LONG path, and p is still within the readable extent (at the end of the header, not past omax).
callers_audited: asn1/d2i.rs check_tlen: len slot initialised to 0; p folded through Cursor::advance_to.
asn1/asn1_gen.rs: hdr_len initialised to 0; breaks on 0x80; pointer difference bounded by the returned p.
asn1/a_d2i_fp.rs: slen initialised to 0; 0x80 is the recoverable TOO_LONG path; offset uses the published p.
asn1/der.rs parse2: len initialised to 0; breaks on 0x80; ep = p + len is only formed after the successful branch.
asn1/prim.rs (two callers): len initialised to 0; 0x80, tag and negative-length guards precede every content read.
pkcs7/pk7_doit.rs: len initialised to 0; the constructed/tag test rejects the 0x80 form before ASN1_OCTET_STRING_set.
scope_item_3_asn1_get_object.authority_quirk: For an indefinite length asn1_get_length does not write *plength; ASN1_get_object then compares the caller's incoming value. Every in-crate caller initialises the slot to 0, and the exported behaviour matches the authority.
scope_item_3_asn1_get_object.test: d2i_asn1_get_object_header_beyond_omax_reports_too_long (declared 5, omax 5 with 3 content bytes: ret has 0x80, len 5, reason ASN1_R_TOO_LONG=155, *pp = start+2 and a real header decodes there)

dispositions.reason: The authority raises TOO_LONG (site 1219) for an unrepresentable hdrlen + plen even when the error/indefinite bit makes it skip the length comparison. A cursor-relative comparison alone would report BAD_OBJECT_HEADER (1226) for that input, changing an observable reason code, so the checked sum and the authority's ordering are preserved. d2i_check_tlen_unrepresentable_sum_keeps_too_long pins reason 155.

dispositions.detail: Five embed_d2i field/template advance sites now share the value cursor; no pointer subtraction or remaining-after arithmetic.
template_ex_d2i narrows its wrapper with Cursor::limit and commits with advance/assignment; no cursor_distance.
Both template_noexp_d2i SET OF/SEQUENCE OF element-advance sites share the field's content cursor.

dispositions.reason: Collected::append reproduces the authority's long-overflow test and then grows a CRYPTO_realloc buffer. Making growth structural needs an allocator-neutral fallible capacity type, which would change the authority's allocation/error sequence, not just a representation.

ex_c2i keeps the authority's (int)len cast and its per-arm comparisons (len != ilen, BIT STRING/OBJECT/INTEGER INT_MAX guards). Replacing the cast with try_from would not remove a guard; the guards are exercised directly at INT_MAX+1.
der.rs is reader-audit scope. The max-accounting invariant proves consumed <= omax; the test pins the error and pointer state. No change manufactured.

dispositions.detail: The decoded-ownership handoff is now structurally single-owner through ContentHandoff, including unwinding.

changes: Added ContentHandoff (owns the collected block from take_raw; releases on Drop unless the codec cleared free_cont) and removed the unsafe Collected::adopt constructor.
Changed free_cont from bool to c_char in d2i_ex_primitive, ex_c2i and the handoff guard; the prim_c2i hook now receives *mut c_char directly.
Threaded one &mut Cursor through embed_d2i, mstring_d2i, template_ex_d2i, template_noexp_d2i and d2i_ex_primitive; each commits the caller's cursor only on success.
Derived the boundary cursor once in item_d2i, ASN1_item_ex_d2i, ASN1_item_d2i_ex and asn1_item_embed_d2i, publishing the caller's in/pp only on success.
Deleted cursor_distance/remaining_after and the interior cursor re-derivations; C1's checked sum is retained to preserve the authority's TOO_LONG reason.
The EXTERN d2i hook remains a raw ABI edge; its answer is folded back with advance_to, and a failing hook no longer publishes partial progress.

negative_control.name: asn1::d2i::tests::d2i_canary_pre_fix_take_raw_handoff_would_leak_on_unwind
negative_control.fires_on: the removed normal-return-only adoption: take_raw cleared the owner and a panic before adoption left the block owned by nobody
negative_control.mechanism: allocates a four-byte block through the seam, constructs ContentHandoff with free_cont=1, unwinds out of the scope under catch_unwind, and asserts the guard's Drop released it (test-only HANDOFF_RELEASES counter). A pre-fix raw handoff would record 0.
negative_control.output: d2i canary: pre-fix take_raw+panic leaked the collected block; post-fix ContentHandoff released it during unwind (releases=1)
negative_control.note: This is a normal-test observation of the Drop path, not a UB detector; only Miri/ASan would observe the pre-fix leak itself.

residuals.finding: A panic after an ASN.1 value has been allocated but before item_ex_d2i_intern's failure free (for example a panic inside a later codec) still leaks the value: guard_ffi catches the unwind but does not run the failure free.
residuals.disposition: Pre-existing, broader than the take_raw handoff fixed here. The handoff block itself is now guard-owned. Requires a failure-atomic/poisoning design for the value slot; Miri/ASan NOT_RUN.

residuals.finding: A caller that shares an ASN1_TLC cache across top-level calls can reuse a header cached by a failed decode. A header that does not fit is refused by the cursor; a fitting stale header can misdecode.
residuals.disposition: Authority-compatible cache contract. No memory unsafety (all advances are bounded). Clearing the caller's cache on failure would be a deliberate behaviour change and was not made.

residuals.finding: EXTERN hooks that advance *in on failure would have that progress published by the authority; this implementation discards it.
residuals.disposition: Deliberate 'no progress on failure' divergence, unobservable for the crate's X509_NAME and X509_PUBKEY hooks.

residuals.finding: The canary observes the Drop path; it does not detect the pre-fix leak itself. No Miri/ASan run verifies the pre-fix read/leak.
C1 (authority checked sum), C5 (collector growth), C6 (authority narrowing cast) and C7 (ASN1_get_object accounting) remain checked-at-site.
residuals.disposition: Recorded above with the reason each cannot be made structural cheaply without changing an observable error reason; C7 is proved sound and tested.

residuals.finding: ASN1_get_object does not write *plength for an indefinite length.
residuals.disposition: Matches the authority; every in-crate caller initialises the slot to 0. A C caller must do the same, as with the authority.
